ticket: Ticket 13 — Wire Jesse FractalReports into NYXEngine + retrain BTC

experiment.wiring: 4 per-file Jesse agents (ContextAgent, RegimeAgent, SetupAgent, EntryAgent) instantiated on NYXEngine.__init__; called via .report() per candidate bar in _generate_candidates; 13 rep_* features merged alongside rule_* proxies

decision_rationale: Per-file Jesse agents are rule-based (ContextAgent SMA fallback) or HSMM-dependent (RegimeAgent, SetupAgent) with HSMM not pre-trained -> neutral-default rep_* values dominate, carrying no predictive signal on BTC 2023.
The GBM with 186 features fits the in-sample perfectly (90.22% accuracy, same as 173-feature baseline) but OOS degrades (Sharpe 9.96 -> 8.04) -- classic noise-feature overfit.
Ticket 13 is explicitly a 'point de vérité': the honest finding is that the current agents do NOT add edge on BTC. Reverting the artefact preserves the validated Ticket 11 edge.

The wiring (NYXEngine._ctx/_reg/_stp/_ent_agent + _build_fractal_report_features) is KEPT because the architectural unification is real: a future ticket can swap in properly trained ML agents (mono-file JesseContextAgent etc. with HSMM pre-training for RegimeAgent / SetupAgent) without touching NYXEngine again.

Persisted artefact = baseline (Ticket 11 values restored via baseline_*.pkl copy-back). reports/BTCUSDT_oos_report.json left as Ticket 13 run for audit; baseline snapshot archived under reports/BTCUSDT_oos_report_baseline_ticket11.json.
next_step_suggestion: Ticket 14 -- pre-train HSMM for RegimeAgent + SetupAgent on BTC 2019 Q1-Q3 slice, OR swap to mono-file JesseContextAgent/etc. (ML-based RandomForest) with proper pre-training slice, then re-run this comparison.
